Uniloculares'' [[E.M.Benn.]] * ''Billardierea'' [[Tom (Tomas) Erik von Post|T.Post]] & [[Otto Kuntze|Kuntze]] orth. var. * ''Labillardiera'' [[Schult.]] [[nom. illeg.]], nom. superfl. * ''Pronaya'' [[Hügel]] ex [[Endl.]] * ''Sollya'' [[Lindl.]] {{hidden end}} }} '''''Billardiera''''', commonly known as '''appleberries''', '''snot berries''', or '''bluebell creepers''',{{cite web |title=''Billardiera'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Billardiera |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra |access-date=27 May 2023}} is a genus of flowering plants in the family, ''[[Pittosporaceae]]'' and is [[endemic]] to Australia. Plants in the genus ''Billardiera'' are woody scramblers, climbers or twiners with elliptic, lance-shaped or linear leaves arranged alternately along the stems, the flowers with petals that are joined to form a tube at the base with spreading lobes, and succulent or fleshy fruit. ==Description== Plants in the genus ''Billardiera'' are woody scramblers, climbers or undershrubs with twining branches up to several metres long. The leaves are [[Leaf#Divisions of the blade|simple]], elliptic, lance-shaped or linear and arranged alternately along the stems. The flowers are arranged singly or in [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]] on the ends of branches and are greenish-yellow to cream-coloured, purple or blue, the [[sepal]]s free from each other. The five petals are much longer than the sepals, sometimes free from each other, or joined at the base to form a tube with spreading lobes. The [[stamen]]s are free from each other, but sometimes have their [[Stamen#Morphology and terminology|anthers]] joined at the tip, encircling the [[Style (botany)|style]]. The fruit is a succulent or fleshy, variously shaped [[berry]] containing many seeds. ==Taxonomy== The genus ''Billardiera'' was first formally described in 1793 by [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]] in his book ''[[A Specimen of the Botany of New Holland]]'', and the first species he described (the [[Type (biology)|type]] species) was ''[[Billardiera scandens]]''. The name, ''Billardiera'' honours [[Jacques Labillardière|Jacques-Julien Houtou de Labillardière]]. ===Species list=== The following is a list of species of ''Billardiera'' accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]] as of May 2023: * ''[[Billardiera coriacea]]'' [[Benth.]] (W.A.) * ''[[Billardiera cymosa]]'' [[F.Muell.]] (S.A., Vic.) * ''[[Billardiera drummondii]]'' ([[Charles François Antoine Morren|C.Morren]]) [[L.Cayzer]] & [[Michael Douglas Crisp|Crisp]] (W.A.) * ''[[Billardiera floribunda]]'' ([[Putt.]]) [[F.Muell.]] – white-flowered billardiera (W.A.) * ''[[Billardiera fraseri]]'' ([[Hook.]]) L.W.Cayzer, Crisp & [[Ian R.H.
